Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: No credible evidence found of a public online tax e-filing/tax portal for Somalia (federal) within this step budget; searched for "Somalia tax portal efiling online tax payment".
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Full-path check (triggered by a signal on the initial light search). The Somalia Revenue Directorate website (revenuedirectorate.gov.so) offers downloadable tax return forms (personal income tax, corporate income tax, withholding tax) as Excel files, but no online e-filing or in-portal e-payment function was found — forms appear to require offline submission. Separately, the Central Bank of Somalia confirms its SOMQR code (launched June 2023, integrated with the National Payment System/SIPS) lets citizens and businesses pay taxes and fees by scanning a QR code, i.e. a tax-payment channel linked to the instant payment system, but this is not itself a dedicated tax-filing portal as the variable defines it. Evidence is genuinely mixed and does not map cleanly onto a single scale value (Unknown/No/Planned/Under development/Yes), so this is flagged for human review rather than guessed. The original 0/Unknown score is plausible but may understate the SOMQR tax-payment capability.
revised_comments: The Somalia Revenue Directorate provides downloadable tax return forms (personal income tax, corporate income tax and withholding tax) via its website, but no online tax-filing or e-payment portal is evident from the site itself. Separately, the Central Bank of Somalia's SOMQR code, integrated with the national payment system, enables citizens and businesses to pay taxes and fees by scanning a QR code, though no dedicated e-filing portal links tax return submission to this payment channel.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: No credible, periodic public performance reporting (monthly/quarterly/annual statistics) specific to SIPS/SPS/NPS found on CBS or SPS websites within this step budget; searched for "payment statistics", "SIPS transaction volume", "NPS annual report".
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown is superseded. The Central Bank of Somalia (CBS) publishes an Annual Statistical Bulletin each June, with editions for 2023, 2024 and 2025 found on centralbank.gov.so/publications, and its June 2024 Policy Brief discloses detailed National Payment System (NPS) performance metrics for 2023 (over one million transactions worth USD 1,752 million; RTGS USD 1,298 million; ACH USD 454 million; 28% year-on-year growth in volume). This is regular, annual public disclosure of payment system usage, transaction volumes and values by the regulator, meeting Value Code 3 (Annual) rather than 0 (Unknown). Fetched and read both the CBS publications page and the June 2024 Policy Brief PDF directly.
revised_comments: The Central Bank of Somalia publishes an Annual Statistical Bulletin each June (2023, 2024 and 2025 editions available) and issues periodic policy briefs disclosing National Payment System performance metrics. The June 2024 policy brief reports that in 2023 the National Payment System processed over one million transactions worth USD 1,752 million, including USD 1,298 million through the Real-Time Gross Settlement system and USD 454 million through the Automated Clearing House, representing year-on-year growth of 28% in volume and 23% in value. This constitutes annual public disclosure of payment system usage, transaction volumes and values by the regulator.

This supports Value Code 1 (No - Confidential) over 0 (Unknown); rules likely exist for participating institutions only. Governance rules appear to be available only to participating banks and the regulator.

Definition: Whether refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons, migrants, and stateless persons can legally access and open digital payment accounts, and practical barriers or enablers for these populations.
Comments: No credible evidence found of formal policies/programs enabling refugees/migrants to access digital payments/mobile money with adapted KYC (e.g., UNHCR programs in Somalia) within this step budget; searched for "Somalia refugee mobile money KYC".
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown is superseded. UNHCR's "Displaced and Disconnected" report (Innovation Service, July 2022) finds that neither refugees nor asylum-seekers in Somalia have legal access to open formal bank accounts, since neither the Federal Government's AML/CFT framework nor Somaliland's 2019 AML/CFT Act recognises refugee identity documents as valid KYC evidence. However, Somalia's 2015 Money Transfer Businesses on Customer Registration Regulations create a tiered KYC framework giving refugees and asylum-seekers legal access to lower-threshold mobile money accounts, and the report notes that in practice mobile money accounts are relatively easy for displaced persons to access. UNCDF's 2023 Somalia payment infrastructure and diagnostic reports corroborate the absence of a unified national ID system, which complicates verification, and recommend digital ID/e-KYC reforms. This is partial rather than full or absent access, supporting Value Code 2 (Partial) rather than 0 (Unknown) or 1 (No). Fetched and read the UNHCR report directly.
revised_comments: Refugees and asylum-seekers in Somalia do not have legal access to open formal bank accounts, since neither the Federal Government's anti-money laundering framework nor Somaliland's 2019 Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act recognises refugee identity documents as valid KYC evidence. However, Somalia's 2015 Money Transfer Businesses on Customer Registration Regulations establish a tiered KYC framework that gives refugees and asylum-seekers legal access to lower-threshold mobile money accounts, and in practice mobile money accounts are relatively easy for displaced persons to obtain. Access therefore remains partial: practical entry points exist through mobile money and money transfer businesses, but full, harmonised legal recognition of refugee identity documents across the formal financial sector is absent.
